title: Noise-driven pseudovorticity multipoles in self-focusing beams with quintic saturation
abstract: We investigate pseudovorticity generation in Gaussian beams undergoing self-focusing under amplitude and phase noise, using the cubic-quintic nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Pseudovorticity, defined as the curl of the optical momentum flux, characterizes local rotational flow in the absence of phase singularities. Our numerical simulations show that thermal amplitude and phase noise induce a multipolar pseudovorticity pattern. Unlike the pure cubic case, where noise asymmetries are radiated away during collapse, the quintic saturation arrests collapse and traps the noise in the resulting soliton. Hence, pseudovorticity multipoles persist, oscillating at the focusing-refocusing period. These results suggest a potential pathway for controlling local optical torque through noise engineering.
summary: The research analyzes the generation of pseudovorticity—a measure of local rotational flow—in self-focusing beams subjected to thermal amplitude and phase noise. By using a cubic-quintic nonlinear model, the authors demonstrate that quintic saturation prevents collapse, trapping noise into persistent, oscillating multipoles. This suggests a novel mechanism for controlling optical torque through careful 'noise engineering'.
main_problem: The study investigates how amplitude and phase noise affect pseudovorticity generation in self-focusing Gaussian beams.
main_result: Quintic saturation arrests collapse, allowing persistent, oscillating multipolar pseudovorticity patterns to form, suggesting noise can control local optical torque.
method: Numerical simulations using the split-step Fourier method on a 2D grid are employed to solve the cubic-quintic nonlinear Schrödinger equation.
model_or_system: The system models self-focusing beam dynamics governed by the (2+1)-dimensional cubic-quintic Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation. Noise is introduced via Gaussian white noise added to both amplitude and phase components of the field.
key_observables: Pseudovorticity ($\omega$), asymmetric intensity residue, angular modal coefficients ($m=1$ dipole, $m=2$ quadrupole) for intensity, phase, and pseudovorticity.
important_parameters: Noise correlation length ($\sigma$), nonlinearity saturation parameter ($\epsilon$), and propagation distance ($z$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the paraxial scalar approximation; the pure cubic case's late-time collapse behavior was limited by spatial resolution.
figures_summary: Figures compare intensity, pseudovorticity evolution for noisy vs. clean beams (Fig. 2); Fig. 3 shows spatial snapshots of asymmetric fields and $\omega$; Figs. 4-7 quantify the mode competition dynamics between dipole and quadrupole components under varying noise statistics.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the model, defines pseudovorticity, simulates the evolution under noise, analyzes the persistence and oscillation of multipoles using modal decomposition (dipole/quadrupole), and concludes by linking input noise statistics to controllable optical torque.
why_interesting: This work bridges nonlinear wave physics with stochastic processes, showing how engineered noise can stabilize or control complex topological features like pseudovorticity in optical systems, relevant for advanced quantum optics applications.
